model: TEC2603-4 and TEC2603-4+PIR Multi-Stage Thermostat (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Rooftop units and split systems with up to two heating and two cooling stages, using the TEC2603-4 thermostat.
summary: The TEC2603-4 is a BACnet MS/TP thermostat for up to two stages of heating and two of cooling. Its object list has system mode, fan mode, occupancy, setpoints, lockout temperatures, the G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2 output status, stage counts, input status and alarms.
notes: Objects from Table 8 on pages 33-36 of the technical bulletin, which also holds separate tables for the other TEC26xx-4 models.
Access comes from the guide's footnotes: read/write, read-only, writable only when out of service (listed as read-only), or writable only after the matching override object is set.
The device object (instance 76aaa, aaa = MS/TP address) is not listed as a point.
Temperatures are listed in °F; the guide also gives the °C range.

source.title: TEC Series BACnet MS/TP Network Temperature and Humidity Controllers Technical Bulletin

integration.summary: Address the thermostat on the BACnet MS/TP trunk, then write System Mode (MV 14), Occupancy (MV 12), Fan Mode (MV 15) and the occupied setpoints (AV 42/43). Read Room Temp, Effective Occupancy, the output status objects and the filter and fan lock alarms.

minimum_points.name: Fan Mode
minimum_points.why: Fan mode: on, auto or smart

integration.enable: Occupancy (MV 12) set to Occupied or Unoccupied overrides local occupancy; Local Occupancy hands it back to the thermostat. System Mode (MV 14) can switch the unit off.
integration.heartbeat: Room Temp Override and Outdoor Temp Override (BV 8 and BV 10) may release on their own after 10 minutes with no BACnet traffic, which ends a BAS-written temperature. Keep writing them while the BAS supplies the value.
integration.remote_sensors: Set Room Temp Override (BV 8) to Override and write Room Temp (AV 7) to supply room temperature; Outdoor Temp Override (BV 10) and Outdoor Temperature (AV 9) work the same way for outdoor air.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only. The address display runs 0 to 254, but use an MS/TP address of 4 to 127.
The thermostat names itself TEC2603-aaa and picks device instance 76aaa, where aaa is the MS/TP address (e.g. 76004).
Leave the thermostat on automatic baud detection; at least one device on the trunk (normally the supervisory controller) needs a fixed baud rate.
gotchas: Writing one setpoint of a heating/cooling pair can make the thermostat move the other one to keep the minimum deadband.
Set the configuration parameters before mapping; the guide recommends re-mapping all objects if configuration changes afterwards.
Output and status objects marked in the guide can only be written when they are out of service; they are listed as read-only.
Frost Alarm (BI 36) works only when Frost Protection (BV 55) is On.
Objects with no access mark in the guide are listed here as read-only.
